rows.source: HSE gas transporter safety cases
rows.verified: A gas conveyor's safety case must be formally accepted by HSE before the dutyholder can convey gas.

rows.source: HSE gas transporter safety cases
rows.verified: Gas-transporter safety cases should be prepared to meet the Gas Safety (Management) Regulations 1996 and HSE's associated guidance.

rows.source: HSE gas transporter safety cases
rows.verified: HSE's Safety Case Assessment Manual guides assessors and provides transparency about assessment standards and timescales.

rows.source: HSE gas transporter safety cases
rows.verified: Each gas conveyor and the Network Emergency Co-ordinator must describe network-safety arrangements in an accepted GSMR safety case.

rows.source: HSE gas transporter safety cases
rows.verified: Minimising the risk of a gas-supply emergency is a key element of the safety case.

rows.source: HSE gas transporter safety cases
rows.verified: HSE inspects gas conveyors to verify that accepted safety-case arrangements are in place and working correctly.

rows.source: HSE gas transporter safety cases
rows.verified: Industry emergency exercises are undertaken annually to test arrangements for potential or actual gas-supply emergencies.

rows.source: HSE gas transporter safety cases
rows.verified: Producers, storage operators, shippers, suppliers and consumers must co-operate as necessary, and some consumers may be directed to stop using gas to protect network pressure.

rows.source: HSE gas transporter safety cases
rows.verified: Gas-supply safety depends on network pressure, demand, supply availability, storage, isolation capability, safety-case controls, participant co-operation and emergency decisions.

rows.source: HSE gas transporter safety cases
rows.verified: Gas-safety-case evidence is network-, operator-, demand-, supply- and scenario-specific and is not an exact parcel-level outage or incident probability.

rows.source: HSE offshore electrical and control systems
rows.verified: Offshore electrical systems must be managed to prevent electric shock, burns, arcing, fire and explosion.

rows.source: HSE offshore electrical and control systems
rows.verified: The offshore control-systems scope includes electrical generation and distribution.

rows.source: HSE offshore electrical and control systems
rows.verified: Safety-instrumented systems include fire and gas detection, emergency shutdown, process shutdown and pressure protection.

rows.source: HSE offshore electrical and control systems
rows.verified: Process-control instrumentation and supervisory control and data acquisition systems form part of offshore safety management.

rows.source: HSE offshore electrical and control systems
rows.verified: Machinery control systems, including drill-floor machinery, require suitable control and interlocking.

rows.source: HSE offshore electrical and control systems
rows.verified: Dynamic-positioning systems are included within the offshore electrical and control-systems topic.

rows.source: HSE offshore electrical and control systems
rows.verified: Heating, ventilation and air-conditioning control and monitoring can be safety-relevant offshore.

rows.source: HSE offshore electrical and control systems
rows.verified: Offshore communications include public-address and general-alarm systems and remote communications.

rows.source: HSE offshore electrical and control systems
rows.verified: Offshore control-system risk depends on architecture, hazardous-area classification, sensors, logic, power supplies, communications, maintenance, proof testing and human response.

rows.source: HSE offshore electrical and control systems
rows.verified: Offshore control-system evidence is installation-, function-, barrier-, equipment- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level major-incident probability.
